openPrerequisites.requirement: Verified merchant identity, exact HTTPS destination and independently inspectable authorization evidence
Source-backed first product and editorial packet
Owner-selected production HTTPS origin and deployment assumptions

approvedArchitecture: Typed, repository-managed catalogue records behind a validated access layer.
Direct merchant links; Picksy never redirects through its own endpoints.
Approved destinations are owned by a merchant record and selected by a stable destination ID.
A destination is an exact HTTPS URL, validated including path and query, with a required authorization-evidence reference.
At most one active offer per product.
One combined product and review page.
External review-source links are labelled and safe.
Published content is driven by the authoritative catalogue, not by page markup.
Synthetic test data is separate from production data.
invariants: The production catalogue stays empty while Gate 3 is unauthorized.
Synthetic fixtures are never imported by production application code or exposed through an environment switch.
Template.txt is unrelated to the product and stays untouched.
Catalogue validation and its tests are not weakened or removed.
No secrets, credentials or tokens are committed.
The site stays noindex and no deployment or indexing change is made without owner authorization.
forbiddenScope: Real merchant, product, review, destination or offer records.
Checkout, payments, accounts, merchant portal, scraping, ingestion or analytics expansion.
Deployment, hosting, production-origin or indexing changes.
Changes that weaken Guardian policy or Guardian security controls.
externalEvidenceBoundaries: A repository value, URL or authorization reference is never proof that merchant or editorial evidence exists.
A reachable affiliate URL does not establish merchant authorization.
Guardian cannot verify external evidence; it reports such evidence as MISSING or UNVERIFIED only.
A Guardian or AI PASS is advisory and never authorizes a Gate, a merge, a publication or a deployment.

severityRules.BLOCKING: A proven violation of a protected invariant. The revision must not merge as it stands.
severityRules.HIGH: A change to protected state or controls, or strong evidence of a violation, that needs an accountable human decision.
severityRules.MEDIUM: A heuristic signal or missing evidence that a human should check.
severityRules.LOW: A minor observation that does not affect the decision.

decisionRules: FAIL when any finding is BLOCKING, or the AI review returns FAIL.
INCONCLUSIVE when any part of the revision could not be reviewed, or the AI review did not complete with a valid structured result. An incomplete review is never reported as PASS or WARN.
WARN when the review is complete and any finding is HIGH or MEDIUM.
PASS only when the review is complete and no finding is above LOW.
The final status is the worst of the deterministic status and the AI status. AI output can never improve a deterministic result.
